title: Amazon AppFlow
description: No-code service that moves data on demand, on schedule or on event between SaaS applications and AWS services.

title: Amazon Athena

title: Amazon Athena for Apache Spark
description: Serverless, interactive Apache Spark sessions in Athena that start quickly and are billed per DPU-hour, used through notebooks, Spark Connect or APIs.

title: Amazon Aurora
description: MySQL- and PostgreSQL-compatible relational database with distributed storage, read replicas, global databases and copy-on-write cloning.

title: Amazon Bedrock
description: Managed API for invoking foundation models from Amazon and third parties, with on-demand, batch, cross-Region and provisioned inference options.

title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
description: Platform for hosting and operating AI agents built with any framework or model, providing isolated runtime sessions, memory, identity, code and browser tools and tracing.

title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations
description: Scores agent sessions, traces and tool calls with built-in, third-party or custom evaluators, online or in batch, and supports A/B tests between agent versions.

title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway
description: Managed MCP endpoint that turns APIs, Lambda functions and existing MCP servers into governed agent tools and can front model providers with rate and token limits.

title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Policy
description: Deterministic rules, written in natural language or a Cedar-compatible language, that decide which tools an agent may call and with which parameters.

title: Amazon Bedrock Agents Classic
description: Original configuration-based Bedrock agent service that orchestrates a model with action groups and knowledge bases.

title: Amazon Bedrock custom models

description: Adapts supported foundation models with fine-tuning, continued pre-training or distillation, and imports externally trained weights for serving.

title: Amazon Bedrock Data Automation
description: Generative AI service that turns documents, images, audio and video into structured fields, summaries and classifications through one API.

title: Amazon Bedrock Evaluations
description: Evaluation jobs that score models and RAG sources against built-in or custom datasets using metrics, LLM-as-a-judge or human reviewers.

title: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
description: Configurable filters that check model inputs and outputs for harmful content, denied topics, banned words, personal data, ungrounded answers and rule violations.

title: Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases
description: Managed retrieval-augmented generation that ingests content, parses and chunks it, embeds and indexes it, and retrieves relevant passages with citations.

title: Amazon Bedrock Prompt management
description: Library for storing prompts with variables, model settings and variants, saving immutable versions and optimising prompts for a chosen model.

title: Amazon CloudWatch
description: Collects metrics, logs and traces from AWS services and applications, with alarms, dashboards, anomaly detection and log queries.

title: Amazon Comprehend
description: Natural language processing API that detects entities, key phrases, sentiment, language and personal data in text, with custom classifiers.

title: Amazon Data Firehose
description: Managed delivery stream that buffers events, optionally transforms them, and writes them to S3, Iceberg tables, Redshift, OpenSearch, Splunk or HTTP endpoints.

title: Amazon DynamoDB
description: Serverless key-value and document database with single-digit millisecond reads and writes, which partitions data automatically as tables grow.

title: Amazon EMR on EC2
description: Managed clusters on EC2 that run Apache Spark, Hive, Trino, Flink, HBase and other open-source frameworks with versioned release labels.

title: Amazon EMR on EKS
description: Runs EMR's Spark runtime as jobs on an existing Amazon EKS cluster so data processing shares Kubernetes capacity with other workloads.

title: Amazon EMR Serverless
description: Serverless option for running Spark and Hive jobs on the EMR runtime without sizing or managing clusters.

title: Amazon EventBridge
description: Serverless event bus, scheduler and point-to-point pipes that route events from AWS services, SaaS partners and applications to targets by rule.

title: Amazon Kendra
description: Enterprise search service that indexes documents from many connectors and returns ranked, permission-filtered results.

title: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams
description: Serverless, sharded event stream that stores ordered records for up to 365 days and lets many consumers read them independently.

title: Amazon Location Service
description: APIs for maps, geocoding, place search, routing, geofencing and device tracking.

title: Amazon Macie
description: Samples and scans S3 objects with managed and custom identifiers to find personal and sensitive data, and evaluates bucket access settings.

title: Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink

description: Managed runtime for Apache Flink applications in Java, Scala, Python or SQL, with checkpoints, scaling and a notebook-based Studio for interactive streaming SQL.

title: Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka
description: Managed Apache Kafka offering provisioned clusters with Standard or Express brokers and a serverless option.

title: Amazon Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow
description: Managed Apache Airflow environments in your VPC that run Python DAGs with autoscaled workers and CloudWatch logging.

title: Amazon MWAA Serverless
description: Deployment option for Amazon MWAA that runs Airflow 3 workflows defined in YAML without a standing environment, charging only for task run time.

title: Amazon Neptune

title: Amazon OpenSearch Service

title: Amazon Q Business
description: Generative AI assistant for employees that answered questions and ran Q Apps over indexed enterprise content.

title: Amazon Quick
description: Workplace AI service combining chat agents, deep research, workflow automation, BI and generated apps over company data and connected applications.

title: Amazon Quick Sight
description: Serverless BI for building interactive dashboards, pixel-perfect paginated reports and embedded analytics, with natural-language questions over curated topics.

title: Amazon Redshift
description: Massively parallel columnar data warehouse, offered as provisioned RA3 clusters with Redshift Managed Storage or as Redshift Serverless.

title: Amazon Redshift auto-copy
description: COPY jobs that watch an S3 prefix and load each new file into a Redshift table once, as it arrives.

title: Amazon Redshift concurrency scaling
description: Adds transient compute automatically when queries queue on a Redshift warehouse and removes it when load drops.

title: Amazon Redshift data sharing
description: Shares live tables and views between Redshift warehouses in the same or other accounts and Regions without copying, so separate compute can read the same data.

title: Amazon Redshift federated query
description: Queries live data in Aurora and RDS PostgreSQL and MySQL databases from Redshift SQL without loading it first.

title: Amazon Redshift materialized views
description: Precomputed query results in Redshift that refresh incrementally where possible and can be used automatically to rewrite matching queries.

title: Amazon Redshift ML
description: Trains and runs machine learning models from Redshift SQL with CREATE MODEL, using SageMaker AI for training and Bedrock models for text tasks.

title: Amazon Redshift row-level security and dynamic data masking
description: Redshift policies that filter rows and mask column values per role at query time, alongside role-based SQL permissions.

title: Amazon Redshift Serverless
description: Deployment option for Redshift that allocates compute in RPUs automatically, scales with load and charges only while queries run.

title: Amazon Redshift Spectrum
description: Lets Redshift query and join open-format files and Iceberg tables in S3 through external schemas in the Glue Data Catalog.

title: Amazon Redshift streaming ingestion
description: Reads Kinesis Data Streams and Kafka topics directly into Redshift materialised views with seconds-level latency, without staging in S3.

title: Amazon S3
aliases: Amazon Simple Storage Service;S3 Object Lock;S3 Access Grants
description: Object storage service that holds files of any size in buckets and is the usual foundation for data lakes on AWS.

title: Amazon S3 Files
description: Presents an existing S3 bucket as a shared file system so file-based applications and agents can read and write the same data that S3 APIs see.

title: Amazon S3 Metadata
description: Captures object metadata for a general purpose bucket into read-only, S3-managed Iceberg tables (journal, live inventory and annotation tables) that can be queried with SQL.

title: Amazon S3 storage classes and S3 Lifecycle
description: Set of S3 storage tiers from Standard to Glacier Deep Archive, with Intelligent-Tiering and lifecycle rules that move or expire objects by age.

title: Amazon S3 Tables
description: S3 bucket type (table buckets) that stores Apache Iceberg tables and runs compaction, snapshot expiry and unreferenced-file removal automatically.

title: Amazon S3 Vectors
description: S3 bucket type (vector buckets) that stores embeddings in vector indexes and answers similarity queries with metadata filters, without provisioned infrastructure.

title: Amazon SageMaker AI inference
description: Model hosting options covering real-time, serverless and asynchronous endpoints and batch transform jobs, with traffic-shifting deployment controls.

title: Amazon SageMaker AI training jobs
description: Managed, ephemeral training jobs that run containers on CPU, GPU or Trainium instances, with distributed training libraries and automatic model tuning.

title: Amazon SageMaker AI with MLflow
description: Managed MLflow, provided as serverless MLflow Apps, for tracking experiments, comparing runs and tracing generative AI applications.

title: Amazon SageMaker Autopilot
description: AutoML API that explores feature processing, algorithms and hyperparameters to produce ranked candidate models for tabular, text, image and time-series tasks.

title: Amazon SageMaker Canvas
description: No-code ML workspace where analysts prepare data, build and evaluate models automatically, and generate predictions.

title: Amazon SageMaker Catalog
description: Business data catalogue in SageMaker Unified Studio where producers publish assets and data products with glossary terms and metadata forms, and consumers search and subscribe.

title: Amazon SageMaker Clarify
description: Processing jobs that compute pre- and post-training bias metrics and SHAP feature attributions for models and datasets.

description: AI assistant in SageMaker Unified Studio notebooks and the query editor that writes SQL and code from natural language, explains its plan and fixes failed queries.

title: Amazon SageMaker Feature Store
description: Feature repository with an online store holding the latest values for low-latency lookup and an append-only offline store in S3 for training.

title: Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth
description: Labelling service that runs annotation jobs for images, text, video and point clouds using private, vendor or automated workforces.

title: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod
description: Persistent, self-healing accelerator clusters orchestrated by Slurm or Amazon EKS for large-scale model training, fine-tuning and inference.

title: Amazon SageMaker JumpStart
description: Hub of open-weight and proprietary foundation models and solution templates that can be fine-tuned and deployed to SageMaker AI endpoints in your account.

title: Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor
description: Scheduled jobs that compare captured endpoint traffic with a baseline to report data quality, model quality, bias and attribution drift.

title: Amazon SageMaker Model Registry
description: Catalogue of versioned model packages grouped by use case, with approval status, metadata, lineage and Model Cards for documentation.

title: Amazon SageMaker Pipelines
description: Serverless workflow service for ML steps such as processing, training, evaluation, registration and deployment, defined in Python.

title: Amazon SageMaker Studio
description: Web-based ML development environment in SageMaker AI offering JupyterLab, Code Editor and RStudio spaces with managed compute.

title: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio
description: Browser-based workbench that brings SQL querying, notebooks, visual ETL, workflows, ML and Bedrock tools together in domains and projects with shared permissions.

title: Amazon Textract

title: Amazon Timestream for InfluxDB

title: Amazon Timestream for LiveAnalytics
description: Serverless time-series database with memory and magnetic tiers and SQL time-series functions.

title: AWS Snowball Edge

title: AWS Step Functions
description: Serverless state-machine service that coordinates AWS service calls, Lambda functions and human approvals with retries and error handling.

title: AWS Transfer Family
description: Managed SFTP, FTPS, FTP and AS2 endpoints that store exchanged files directly in S3 or EFS.

title: AWS Transform
description: Agentic AI service that plans and carries out migration and modernisation work for mainframe, VMware and .NET workloads.

title: AWS zero-ETL integrations

title: chDB
description: In-process OLAP engine built on ClickHouse that runs inside Python, Go, Rust, Node.js or C/C++ programs, with a pandas-compatible DataStore API.

title: ClickHouse access control (users, roles, row policies, masking policies, settings profiles and quotas)
description: SQL-managed access entities that grant privileges to roles, filter rows per user, mask column values per user, and cap settings and resource use per user or role.

title: ClickHouse Agents
description: Managed agent service in ClickHouse Cloud with a chat interface, no-code agent builder, skills, memory, sandboxed code execution and MCP tool access, using Claude models by default.

title: ClickHouse AI functions
description: SQL functions such as aiGenerate, aiClassify, aiExtract, aiTranslate, aiRedact and aiEmbed that call an LLM or embedding endpoint for each row.

title: ClickHouse Cloud backups and BACKUP/RESTORE

description: Connects ClickHouse Cloud services and ClickPipes to customer virtual networks over the cloud providers' private endpoint services, and restricts public access with IP filters.

description: Turns a saved, parameterised SQL query in the Cloud console into an authenticated HTTP endpoint that returns results in any ClickHouse format.

description: Browser workspace for writing and sharing queries, charting results, building parameterised dashboards from saved queries and asking an AI assistant to write SQL or explore data.

title: ClickHouse Cloud usage breakdown and spend alerts
description: Console usage breakdown by service and cost category, a usage cost API, and organisation spend alerts at set thresholds of committed or budgeted spend.

title: ClickHouse Cloud Warehouses (compute-compute separation)

title: ClickHouse data skipping indexes

title: ClickHouse data source plugin for Grafana
description: Signed Grafana data source with a query builder for building dashboards and exploring logs and traces stored in ClickHouse.

title: ClickHouse DataLakeCatalog database engine
description: Database engine that connects to an external lakehouse catalogue and exposes its tables as ClickHouse tables for querying and joining.

title: ClickHouse dictionaries
description: In-memory key-value lookups loaded from ClickHouse tables, external databases, HTTP or files, refreshed on a set lifetime and queried with dictGet functions or as tables.

title: ClickHouse geo data types and functions

title: ClickHouse incremental materialized views
description: Insert triggers that run a query over each newly inserted block and write the results to a target table, usually an AggregatingMergeTree or SummingMergeTree that merges partial aggregates.

title: ClickHouse integration table engines and table functions
description: Engines and functions such as postgresql, mysql, mongodb, s3, url, jdbc, odbc and arrowflight that read from and write to external databases and storage directly in SQL.

title: ClickHouse interfaces and client drivers
description: HTTP, native TCP, gRPC and Arrow Flight interfaces, MySQL and PostgreSQL wire-protocol compatibility, and official clients including JDBC, ODBC, ADBC, Python, Go, Node.js, Rust, C++ and .NET.

title: ClickHouse JSON, Dynamic and Variant data types
description: Column types that store semi-structured JSON as typed sub-columns per path, and values whose type varies from row to row, without flattening them first.

title: ClickHouse Kafka table engine
description: Table engine that consumes Kafka topics as a consumer group and, with a materialised view, writes messages continuously into MergeTree tables; RabbitMQ and NATS engines work the same way.

title: ClickHouse Keeper
description: Raft-based coordination service, compatible with the ZooKeeper client protocol, that coordinates replication, distributed DDL and queue engines.

title: ClickHouse lightweight updates and deletes
description: Changes or removes individual rows in MergeTree tables by writing small patch parts or a deleted-row mask that queries apply at once, instead of rewriting whole parts.

title: ClickHouse Managed Postgres
description: Managed PostgreSQL on local NVMe storage with high availability, read replicas and point-in-time recovery, wired to ClickHouse through built-in CDC and the pg_clickhouse extension.

title: ClickHouse MCP server (open-source and Remote MCP in Cloud)
description: Model Context Protocol servers that let AI assistants list ClickHouse databases and tables and run read-only queries, including a managed remote endpoint for ClickHouse Cloud.

title: ClickHouse projections
description: Hidden, automatically maintained copies of a table with a different sort order or pre-aggregation that the optimiser picks when they reduce the data read.

title: ClickHouse query cache
description: Stores the results of SELECT queries in memory, or optionally on disk, and serves repeats until a time to live expires.

title: ClickHouse Query Insights and system tables
description: Console views of query volume, latency and errors built on system.query_log, alongside system tables, Cloud monitoring dashboards and Prometheus endpoints that expose server, query and ClickPipes metrics.

title: ClickHouse refreshable materialized views
description: Views that rerun a full query on a schedule and replace or append to a target table, with optional dependencies between views.

title: ClickHouse server
description: Open-source column-oriented SQL database that runs analytical queries over very large tables with vectorised, parallel execution on single servers or sharded and replicated clusters.

title: ClickHouse Terraform provider
description: Official Terraform provider for ClickHouse Cloud services, scaling, private endpoints, organisation roles and API keys, ClickPipes, ClickStack resources and Managed Postgres.

title: ClickHouse text indexes (full-text search)
description: Inverted indexes on string, array and map columns with configurable tokenisers that answer token, phrase and pattern searches without scanning.

title: ClickHouse TimeSeries table engine
description: Experimental engine that stores Prometheus-style metrics as samples, tags and metric tables and accepts Prometheus remote-write and remote-read traffic.

title: ClickHouse TTL (time to live)
description: Table and column rules that delete, roll up, recompress or move data once it reaches a given age, applied during background merges.

title: ClickHouse user-defined functions
description: Extends ClickHouse with SQL lambda functions, executable functions that call external scripts such as Python over standard input and output, and experimental WebAssembly functions.

title: ClickHouse vector similarity indexes
description: HNSW indexes on embedding columns for approximate nearest-neighbour search with L2, cosine or dot-product distance, alongside exact brute-force search and the QBit type.

title: ClickHouse workload scheduling
description: Divides CPU, disk I/O, memory and query slots between a hierarchy of SQL-defined workloads using priorities, weights and limits.

title: clickhouse-local
description: Mode of the ClickHouse binary that runs SQL over local or remote files and piped data without starting a server.

title: ClickPipes

title: ClickPipes database connectors (Postgres CDC, MySQL CDC, MongoDB CDC, BigQuery)

title: ClickStack

title: dbt-clickhouse adapter
description: ClickHouse-supported dbt adapter that builds views, tables, incremental and microbatch models, materialised views and dictionaries in ClickHouse.

title: Langfuse
description: LLM engineering platform that traces model and agent calls, runs evaluations and experiments on datasets, and versions prompts, available self-hosted or as Langfuse Cloud.

title: MergeTree table engine family

title: S3Queue and AzureQueue table engines
description: Table engines that watch an S3 or Azure Blob path and load new files in the background through a materialised view, tracking which files have been processed in Keeper.

title: SharedMergeTree
description: Cloud-native counterpart of the MergeTree family that keeps table data and metadata in shared object storage and coordinates replicas through Keeper instead of copying data between them.

description: Native Apache Iceberg v2 table support across Spark, Hive, Impala, Trino, Flink and NiFi, including time travel, partition evolution and row-level changes.

title: Cloudera Observability

title: Cloudera Replication Manager
description: Service that schedules replication of HDFS, Hive, Iceberg and HBase data and metadata between clusters and to cloud storage.

title: Cloudera Shared Data Experience (SDX)
description: Common security and governance layer, built on Apache Ranger, Apache Atlas and Apache Knox, applied to every engine on the same data.

title: Cloudera Streaming Analytics
description: Apache Flink distribution with SQL Stream Builder, a console for writing continuous SQL jobs and materialised views over streams.

title: Cloudera Streams Messaging
description: Cloudera's Apache Kafka distribution with Schema Registry, Streams Messaging Manager, Streams Replication Manager and Cruise Control.

title: Agent Bricks
description: Databricks' platform for developing agents. It brings together agent hosting, sandboxed code execution, memory, MCP tools, retrieval, tracing, evaluation and governed model access.

title: Agent Bricks Knowledge Assistant and Supervisor Agent
description: No-code agents. Knowledge Assistant answers questions over documents with citations, and Supervisor Agent coordinates Genie Agents, tables, AI Search indexes, MCP servers and other agents.

title: Databricks Agent Evaluation (MLflow GenAI evaluation)
description: Evaluates agents and LLM applications against datasets, using built-in and custom scorers, LLM judges and human feedback, and also monitors production traces.

title: Databricks Agent Runtime and Agent Bricks CLI
description: Serverless hosting for code-based agents on Databricks Apps, with durable run state, an authenticated endpoint, a service-principal identity and MLflow tracing, deployed with the agentbricks CLI.

title: Databricks agentic code converter
description: A Genie Code-based migration project that converts T-SQL, Snowflake, Redshift, Oracle, BigQuery and Teradata SQL into Databricks SQL or DataFrame notebooks.

title: Databricks AI Functions
description: SQL and Python functions that call models over table data. They include ai_query, ai_extract, ai_classify, ai_summarize, ai_translate, ai_mask, ai_forecast and ai_similarity, with ai_search, ai_prep_search and ai_transcribe in Beta.

title: Databricks AI Runtime
description: Serverless GPU compute for deep learning, used to train and fine-tune models on one or many GPUs with PyTorch DDP and FSDP, DeepSpeed or Ray.

title: Databricks AI Search
formerly: Mosaic AI Vector Search;Databricks Vector Search
description: A managed vector and full-text search service. Delta Sync indexes stay in step with source tables and can compute embeddings, and hybrid retrieval is supported.

title: Databricks AI/BI dashboards
description: Built-in dashboards with AI-assisted authoring, cross-filtering and drill-through. They can be shared at account level, sent on schedules by email or Slack, and embedded in external applications.

title: Databricks ai_parse_document
description: An AI Function that extracts text, tables and layout elements from PDFs, images and office documents stored in volumes, returning structured output.

title: Databricks Apps
description: Serverless hosting for Python and Node.js web applications (for example Streamlit, Dash, Gradio and React) that run inside the workspace with Unity Catalog, SQL warehouse and OAuth integration.

title: Databricks Auto Loader
description: A Structured Streaming source (cloudFiles) that discovers new files in cloud storage and processes each one exactly once, with schema inference, schema evolution and a rescued-data column.

title: Databricks automatic identity management
description: Synchronises users, groups and service principals from Microsoft Entra ID or Okta on demand, without configuring SCIM provisioning. It works alongside SSO, OAuth and service principals.

title: Databricks AutoML
description: Generates baseline classification, regression and forecasting models through a UI or Python API, and produces editable notebooks for each trial.

title: Databricks budgets
description: Account-level spend tracking at list price, filtered by workspace, resource type and tags. You set monthly thresholds with email alerts and, for Unity Gateway, optional per-user blocking.

title: Databricks Catalog Explorer
description: The workspace UI for browsing and managing Unity Catalog assets. It shows schemas, permissions, lineage, popularity, table health indicators and AI-generated comments.

title: Databricks catalog federation
description: Mounts external catalogues such as Hive metastore, AWS Glue, Snowflake Horizon and Salesforce Data 360 as foreign catalogs, read from object storage under Unity Catalog governance.

title: Databricks change data feed
description: Records row-level inserts, updates and deletes on Delta tables so downstream jobs and streams can read only the changes.

title: Databricks classic compute (Databricks Runtime clusters)
description: All-purpose and job clusters, plus instance pools, running Databricks Runtime in the customer's cloud account. You choose instance types, autoscaling and access mode.

title: Databricks Clean Rooms
description: Isolated serverless environments where up to ten organisations share data through OpenSharing and run notebooks that every party has approved. No party sees the others' underlying data.

title: Databricks compliance security profile
description: A workspace setting that applies a hardened, FIPS-validated compute image, enhanced security monitoring and encrypted egress, required for HIPAA, PCI-DSS, FedRAMP and similar regulated data.

title: Databricks Connect
description: A client library built on Spark Connect. Python, Scala and R DataFrame code written in an IDE or application runs on remote Databricks compute, including serverless.

title: Databricks customer-managed keys
description: Customer-held cloud KMS keys that encrypt control-plane data (notebooks, secrets, queries), workspace storage and, at catalogue level, Unity Catalog managed data.

title: Databricks Data Classification
description: A serverless agent that scans Unity Catalog tables incrementally, detects sensitive data such as PII and payment-card data, and tags the columns.

title: Databricks data profiling
description: Computes profile and drift metrics for a table over time as snapshot, time-series or inference profiles, and stores them in Delta tables with a generated dashboard.

title: Databricks data quality monitoring anomaly detection
description: Monitors every table in a schema with one setting. It learns each table's update and volume patterns, flags late or incomplete tables, and suggests root causes using lineage.

title: Databricks Declarative Automation Bundles
description: A Databricks CLI feature that defines jobs, pipelines, dashboards, apps, serving endpoints, AI Search, Lakebase and other resources in YAML with per-target settings. The CLI then validates, plans and deploys them from CI/CD.

title: Databricks Discover
description: A curated browsing page that groups governed tables, dashboards, notebooks and Genie Agents into business domains and subdomains, with highlighted assets chosen by admins and AI recommendations.

title: Databricks Excel Add-in
description: A Microsoft Excel add-in for querying governed Databricks tables and metric views from a workbook.

title: Databricks Feature Store
description: A feature registry in Unity Catalog that stores features in primary-keyed Delta tables, with point-in-time training set creation, automatic lookup at inference and lineage to models.

title: Databricks Feature Views
description: Declarative feature definitions, including time-windowed aggregations over batch, streaming and request-time data, for which Databricks builds and runs the pipelines.

title: Databricks Foundation Model APIs
description: Databricks-hosted proprietary and open language and embedding models, available pay-per-token or with provisioned throughput. They are exposed as governed model services in the system.ai schema.

title: Databricks Free Edition
description: A no-cost, serverless-only, quota-limited Databricks environment for learning and experiments. It includes notebooks, SQL, Lakeflow, dashboards, Genie, Genie Code and Lakebase.

title: Databricks Git folders
description: Workspace folders backed by a Git repository. Users clone, branch, commit, merge and resolve conflicts from the UI, the API or Git CLI commands.

title: Databricks Governance Hub
description: An account-level console that brings together data health and governance coverage, tag usage, AI usage and spend, and cost drivers, with recommended actions.

title: Databricks governed tags
description: Account-level tag definitions with controlled values and assignment permissions, applied to Unity Catalog objects and workspace assets and used by ABAC, classification and cost reporting.

title: Databricks Iceberg reads (UniForm)
description: Generates Iceberg metadata asynchronously for Delta tables so that Iceberg clients can read them without copying the data.

title: Databricks inference tables
description: Logs requests and responses from serving endpoints, foundation model calls and agents to Unity Catalog Delta tables for monitoring, audit and retraining.

title: Databricks JDBC, ODBC and ADBC drivers
description: Client drivers and connectors (JDBC, ODBC, ADBC, Python, Go and Node.js) plus the SQL Statement Execution REST API, used to query Databricks SQL warehouses from tools and code.

title: Databricks Lakehouse Real-Time
description: A serverless SQL warehouse type tuned for sub-second reads of Unity Catalog tables by many concurrent users and applications.

title: Databricks liquid clustering
description: A data layout method that clusters table files by key columns you can change at any time, replacing partitioning and Z-ordering. With CLUSTER BY AUTO, Databricks chooses the keys from query history.

title: Databricks managed disaster recovery
description: Replicates Unity Catalog metadata, managed table data and workspace assets to a secondary region, behind a stable URL that survives failover.

title: Databricks managed MCP servers
description: Hosted Model Context Protocol servers that expose Unity Catalog functions, AI Search indexes, Genie Agents and Genie One to agents as tools. External MCP servers can also be registered as Unity Catalog MCP services.

title: Databricks Marketplace
description: An exchange for publishing and finding datasets, AI models, notebooks, apps and MCP servers, either publicly or through private exchanges, delivered with OpenSharing.

title: Databricks Model Serving
description: Serverless CPU and GPU endpoints for serving custom MLflow models, Databricks-hosted foundation models and external models in real time, with traffic splitting between model versions.

title: Databricks notebooks
description: Collaborative notebooks with Python, SQL, Scala and R cells, comments, version history, widgets and visualisations that can be scheduled as jobs.

title: Databricks Online Feature Store
description: A Lakebase-backed store that publishes feature tables for millisecond lookups by Model Serving endpoints and feature serving endpoints.

title: Databricks OpenSharing
description: Live sharing of tables, views, materialised views, metric views, volumes, models and notebooks with other Databricks accounts, or tabular data with any client through an open protocol, without copying.

title: Databricks Photon
description: Databricks' native C++ vectorised execution engine. It runs Spark SQL and DataFrame operations on columnar batches and falls back to Spark for operations it does not support.

title: Databricks predictive optimization
description: Runs OPTIMIZE, VACUUM and ANALYZE automatically on Unity Catalog managed tables and chooses liquid clustering keys, based on how each table is used.

title: Databricks serverless compute
description: Databricks-managed, versionless compute for notebooks, jobs and pipelines. It starts quickly, scales automatically and is billed in DBUs per use.

title: Databricks serverless egress control
description: Account-level network policies that limit which destinations serverless compute, apps and model serving can reach, used with network connectivity configurations and private endpoint rules.

title: Databricks serverless usage policies
description: Sets of tags applied automatically to the serverless usage of the users assigned to a policy, so that spend from notebooks, jobs, pipelines, serving, apps and Lakebase can be attributed.

title: Databricks spatial SQL (GEOMETRY and GEOGRAPHY)
description: Native GEOMETRY and GEOGRAPHY types with ST_ functions for constructing, measuring, relating and transforming spatial data, plus H3 functions.

title: Databricks SQL
description: The data warehousing product on the lakehouse. It includes the SQL editor, queries, ANSI SQL engine, SQL transformations, materialised views and BI connectivity, running on SQL warehouses.

title: Databricks SQL alerts
description: Scheduled queries that evaluate a condition and send email, Slack or webhook notifications when it is met.

title: Databricks SQL warehouses (serverless, pro and classic)
description: Compute for Databricks SQL in serverless, pro or classic form. Serverless warehouses start in seconds and use intelligent workload management to scale and queue queries.

title: Databricks system tables
description: Databricks-hosted tables in the system catalog that cover billing, audit, lineage, compute, query history, jobs, pipelines, serving, MLflow, classification, data quality and Lakebase activity.

title: Databricks table clone (shallow and deep clone)
description: Copies a table at a given version. A shallow clone copies only metadata and points at the source files, while a deep clone copies the data as well.

title: Databricks Terraform provider
description: A Terraform provider (databricks/databricks) that manages workspaces, Unity Catalog objects, permissions, compute, jobs and other Databricks resources as code.

title: Databricks VARIANT data type
description: A binary type for semi-structured data such as JSON that is queried without a fixed schema, with shredding into columns for faster reads.

title: Delta Lake on Databricks
description: Databricks' managed implementation of Delta Lake tables, with ACID commits, MERGE, UPDATE and DELETE, schema enforcement, time travel, deletion vectors and type widening.

title: Genie Agents
description: Domain-specific chat interfaces that analysts curate with tables, metric views, example SQL and instructions. They answer business questions in natural language with SQL, tables and charts.

title: Genie Code
description: An AI coding and data agent in notebooks, the SQL editor, the pipelines editor, dashboards and MLflow. It plans, writes and runs code, fixes errors and builds pipelines and dashboards, using Unity Catalog context and the user's permissions.

title: Genie One
description: A simplified interface for business users that combines chat across governed data, dashboards and apps in one place, available in the browser, desktop, Excel and Google Sheets.

title: Lakebase
description: Fully managed Postgres in the Databricks platform. Compute is separate from storage, and it offers autoscaling, scale-to-zero, copy-on-write branching, instant point-in-time restore and read replicas.

title: Lakebridge
description: A Databricks Labs migration toolkit. It assesses legacy warehouse and ETL estates, transpiles their SQL and ETL code to Databricks, and reconciles the migrated data against the source.

title: Lakeflow Connect
description: Managed connectors that ingest data incrementally from SaaS applications, databases (including change data capture), file sources and message buses into Unity Catalog tables, running on serverless Lakeflow pipelines.

title: Lakeflow Designer
description: A visual, no-code canvas where analysts build data preparation flows from operators or natural-language prompts. The flows are backed by generated code governed in Unity Catalog.

title: Lakeflow Jobs
description: Built-in orchestrator that runs dependency graphs of notebooks, pipelines, SQL, dbt and other tasks on schedules or on file-arrival, table-update and continuous triggers, with retries and loops.

title: Lakeflow pipelines
formerly: Delta Live Tables;Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines;Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines
description: A declarative framework in which you define streaming tables, materialised views and flows in SQL or Python. The platform then works out dependencies, incremental refresh, retries and infrastructure.

title: Lakeflow pipelines expectations
description: Declarative data quality constraints on pipeline datasets. For each failing record you choose to warn, drop it or fail the update, and the results are recorded in the pipeline event log.

title: Lakeguard
description: Isolation technology that sandboxes each user's code and UDFs away from the Spark engine and from other users, so shared compute can enforce Unity Catalog row filters and column masks.

title: Lakehouse Federation (query federation)
description: Read-only queries against external databases such as PostgreSQL, Oracle, SQL Server, Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift and Teradata through Unity Catalog foreign catalogs, with query pushdown.

title: Managed MLflow on Databricks
description: MLflow 3 hosted by Databricks, with experiment and run tracking, logged models, prompt management and deployment jobs, all integrated with Unity Catalog permissions and lineage.

title: MLflow Tracing on Databricks
description: Records each step of agent and LLM calls, including inputs, outputs, latency, tokens and feedback, and stores the traces in Unity Catalog tables that can be queried with SQL.

title: Models in Unity Catalog
description: The MLflow model registry hosted in Unity Catalog, with versions, aliases, permissions, tags and lineage to training data and features shared across workspaces.

title: Private Link for Databricks
description: AWS PrivateLink, Azure Private Link and Private Service Connect connectivity for front-end access, classic compute to the control plane, and inbound access to serverless services such as Lakebase and Zerobus Ingest.

title: Secrets in Unity Catalog
description: Credentials stored as governed Unity Catalog securables under a catalog.schema.secret name, with grants and audit.

title: Unity Catalog
description: The account-wide catalogue and governance layer for tables, volumes, functions, models, AI services and connections. It provides a three-level namespace, SQL privileges, audit and workspace bindings.

title: Unity Catalog attribute-based access control (ABAC)
description: Policies attached at catalogue, schema or table level that use governed tags and user attributes to apply row filters, column masks and dynamic grants automatically.

title: Unity Catalog data lineage
description: Captures table- and column-level lineage automatically for queries, notebooks, jobs, pipelines, dashboards and models. External sources and BI tools can be registered so they appear in the same graph.

title: Unity Catalog functions (UDFs)
description: SQL, Python, Scala and Java user-defined functions registered and governed in Unity Catalog. They run on serverless and standard compute with sandboxing.

title: Unity Catalog Iceberg REST Catalog API
description: An Iceberg REST catalogue endpoint with credential vending. Spark, Flink, Trino, Snowflake and other engines can use it to read and write Unity Catalog tables.

title: Unity Catalog managed Iceberg tables
description: Apache Iceberg tables (v1 to v3) that Unity Catalog manages, with compaction, snapshot expiry and liquid clustering. Databricks and external engines can read and write them through the Iceberg REST catalogue.

title: Unity Catalog managed tables
description: Delta or Iceberg tables whose storage location, file layout, maintenance and lifecycle Unity Catalog manages, including on Databricks-managed default storage.

title: Unity Catalog metric views
description: YAML- or SQL-defined semantic objects that keep measures apart from dimensions. They are registered in Unity Catalog and queried from SQL, dashboards, Genie and external BI tools.

title: Unity Catalog volumes
description: Governed, path-addressable storage for non-tabular files such as documents, images, libraries and landing data. Volumes can be managed or external.

title: Unity Gateway
formerly: Mosaic AI Gateway;Databricks AI Gateway;Unity AI Gateway
description: A governance and routing layer in Unity Catalog for model, MCP and agent traffic, with provider fallbacks, rate and consumption limits, guardrails, inference logging and budgets.

title: Zerobus Ingest
description: A serverless push API that writes records straight into Unity Catalog Delta tables. Clients can use gRPC SDKs, REST, OpenTelemetry (OTLP), MQTT or Kafka-compatible producers, and no message broker is needed.

title: Agent Platform AutoML
description: Trains tabular, image and video models from labelled data with automatic feature engineering, architecture search and tuning.

title: Agent Platform Endpoints
description: Managed online prediction endpoints, plus batch prediction jobs, for serving registered models with autoscaling, GPUs and traffic splitting between model versions.

title: Agent Platform Feature Store
description: Feature management that uses BigQuery tables as the offline store and syncs selected features to online stores for low-latency serving.

title: Agent Platform Managed Training
formerly: Vertex AI Training;Vertex AI custom training
description: Runs custom training jobs in prebuilt or custom containers on CPUs, GPUs or TPUs, including multi-node distributed training and hyperparameter tuning.

title: Agent Platform Model Evaluation
description: Computes evaluation metrics for registered models on test data, including data and model bias metrics, and, with Explainable AI, gives feature attributions for predictions.

title: Agent Platform Model Registry
description: Central registry for versioning custom, AutoML and BigQuery ML models, with aliases and deployment to endpoints or batch jobs.

title: Agent Platform Pipelines
description: Serverless execution of Kubeflow Pipelines and TFX workflows, with each run's artefacts and parameters recorded in ML Metadata.

title: Agent Platform RAG Engine
description: Managed retrieval-augmented generation service that ingests, chunks and embeds documents into a corpus and retrieves context for Gemini calls.

title: Agent Platform Vector Search
formerly: Vertex AI Vector Search;Vertex AI Matching Engine
description: Managed approximate nearest-neighbour index service based on ScaNN for low-latency similarity search over billions of vectors.

title: Agent Platform Workbench
description: Managed JupyterLab instances with configurable CPUs, GPUs and Google Cloud integrations for data science and ML development.

title: AlloyDB for PostgreSQL
description: PostgreSQL-compatible database with a disaggregated storage layer, columnar engine for analytical queries and built-in vector search and AI functions.

title: Apigee
description: API management platform for publishing, securing, rate-limiting and monitoring APIs, including APIs that expose data products and LLM endpoints.

title: Assured Workloads
description: Applies controls for data location, personnel access and supported services to folders so workloads meet regulatory regimes such as FedRAMP, CJIS and EU sovereignty requirements.

title: BigQuery
description: Serverless analytical database that runs GoogleSQL over managed and open-format tables with storage and compute billed and scaled separately.

title: BigQuery BI Engine
description: In-memory cache in front of BigQuery that speeds up dashboard-style SQL queries, sized as a regional memory reservation.

title: BigQuery change data capture
description: Applies streamed upserts and deletes, keyed on a declared primary key, to BigQuery tables in the background with a configurable staleness bound.

title: BigQuery change history (APPENDS and CHANGES)
description: Table-valued functions that return rows appended to, or changed in, a table over a time range so downstream jobs can process only the delta.

title: BigQuery continuous queries
description: Long-running SQL statements that process rows as they arrive in a table and write results to BigQuery or Iceberg tables, Pub/Sub, Bigtable or Spanner.

title: BigQuery conversational analytics
description: Natural-language question answering over BigQuery tables, views, graphs and Lakehouse tables through configurable data agents with instructions, glossary terms and verified queries.

title: BigQuery data canvas
description: Visual canvas in BigQuery where users chain search, SQL, chart and insight nodes, driven by natural-language prompts to Gemini.

title: BigQuery data clean rooms
description: Built on BigQuery sharing, lets several parties contribute data that others can query only through analysis rules or approved query templates.

title: BigQuery Data Engineering Agent
description: Gemini agent in BigQuery pipelines and Dataform that writes or changes pipeline code (SQLX) from natural-language requests and investigates failed runs.

title: BigQuery data masking
description: Masks column values at query time according to data policies, using rules such as hashing, nullifying, partial masking or custom masking routines.

title: BigQuery data preparation
description: Visual, Gemini-assisted editor for cleaning, joining and reshaping BigQuery data that saves its steps as runnable SQLX.

title: BigQuery Data Transfer Service
description: Scheduled, managed loads into BigQuery from Google marketing products, SaaS applications, other warehouses, databases and cloud object stores.

title: BigQuery DataFrames
description: Python library (bigframes) offering pandas- and scikit-learn-style APIs that compile to BigQuery SQL so data stays in BigQuery.

title: BigQuery editions
description: Slot-based capacity model in Standard, Enterprise and Enterprise Plus tiers, with autoscaling reservations, optional baseline slots and one- or three-year commitments.

title: BigQuery EXPORT DATA
description: SQL statement that writes query results to Cloud Storage files or directly into Bigtable, Spanner, Pub/Sub and AlloyDB.

title: BigQuery external tables and load jobs
description: Reads or loads Parquet, ORC, Avro, JSON and CSV files from Cloud Storage, including Hive-partitioned layouts, as queryable external tables or native tables.

title: BigQuery federated queries
description: Sends queries from BigQuery to Cloud SQL, AlloyDB, Spanner and SAP Datasphere through connections and joins the results with BigQuery data.

title: BigQuery generative AI functions
description: SQL functions such as AI.GENERATE, AI.GENERATE_TABLE, AI.IF, AI.CLASSIFY, AI.SCORE, AI.AGG and AI.EMBED that call Gemini and partner models over table rows and unstructured objects.

title: BigQuery geospatial analytics
description: GEOGRAPHY type, spatial functions and spatial clustering for storing and analysing points, lines and polygons in BigQuery.

title: BigQuery Graph
description: Defines property graphs over existing BigQuery tables and queries them with ISO GQL, without copying data.

title: BigQuery INFORMATION_SCHEMA views
description: System views exposing jobs, slot usage, reservations, storage, table metadata and replication state as queryable tables.

title: BigQuery managed disaster recovery
description: Cross-region dataset replication paired with failover reservations so compute and storage can be switched to a secondary region in a hard or soft failover.

title: BigQuery managed storage
description: Internal columnar storage for native BigQuery tables, with automatic compression, replication, partitioning, clustering and transactional writes.

title: BigQuery materialized views
description: Precomputed query results that BigQuery refreshes incrementally and uses to rewrite matching queries automatically.

title: BigQuery Migration Service
description: Tooling for moving warehouses to BigQuery, covering assessment, batch and interactive SQL translation, data transfer and validation.

title: BigQuery ML
description: Creates, trains, evaluates and runs machine learning models with SQL inside BigQuery, including imported and remote models.

title: BigQuery object tables and ObjectRef
description: Exposes files in Cloud Storage as rows of metadata (object tables) or as ObjectRef values inside ordinary tables so images, documents and audio can be governed and processed with SQL.

title: BigQuery Omni
description: Runs BigQuery queries on data held in Amazon S3 or Azure Blob Storage, using BigQuery-managed compute in the corresponding AWS or Azure region.

title: BigQuery pipelines
description: Console-built, Dataform-backed pipelines that run SQL, notebook, data preparation and SQLX tasks in dependency order on a schedule.

title: BigQuery policy tags
description: Hierarchical taxonomies of tags attached to columns that drive column-level access control and data masking policies.

title: BigQuery row-level security
description: Row access policies that filter which rows of a table each user or group can see, using SQL filter expressions and optional lookup subqueries.

title: BigQuery search indexes
description: Indexes text and JSON columns so the SEARCH function and equality or LIKE filters can find matching rows without full scans.

title: BigQuery sharing
description: Data exchange service where publishers list datasets, views, models and Pub/Sub topics for subscribers, who get linked read-only copies without data duplication.

title: BigQuery Storage Write API
description: High-throughput API for streaming or batch-committing rows into BigQuery tables with exactly-once semantics, readable within seconds.

title: BigQuery Studio
description: Workspace in the BigQuery console that combines the SQL editor, Colab Enterprise notebooks, Spark sessions, data canvas and saved assets.

title: BigQuery table clones
description: Writable copies of a table that share storage with the base table and are billed only for data that later changes in either.

title: BigQuery table snapshots
description: Read-only, point-in-time copies of a table that store only the bytes that differ from the base table and can be kept beyond the time travel window.

title: BigQuery tables for Apache Iceberg
formerly: BigLake tables for Apache Iceberg in BigQuery;BigLake managed tables
description: BigQuery-managed tables stored as Apache Iceberg files in your Cloud Storage bucket, with BigQuery handling writes, clustering, compaction and garbage collection.

title: BigQuery time travel
description: Lets you query or restore a table as it was at any point within a configurable window of two to seven days, backed by a further fail-safe period.

title: BigQuery user-defined functions
description: Extends GoogleSQL with SQL, JavaScript and Python UDFs, remote functions on Cloud Run, stored procedures and stored procedures for Apache Spark.

title: BigQuery vector search
description: Stores embeddings in BigQuery tables and finds nearest neighbours with VECTOR_SEARCH and AI.SEARCH, optionally using IVF or TreeAH vector indexes.

title: BigQuery workload management
description: Reservations, assignments, idle-slot sharing, target concurrency, query queues and reservation groups that divide slot capacity between projects and workload types.

title: Bigtable
description: Wide-column NoSQL database for very high-throughput, low-latency reads and writes, often used for time series, events and feature serving.

title: Cloud Data Fusion
description: Visual, plugin-based integration service built on open-source CDAP for designing batch and real-time pipelines that run on Managed Service for Apache Spark.

title: Cloud Run
description: Serverless platform for running containers, functions and jobs that scale to zero, often used for data APIs, remote functions and data applications.

title: Cloud SQL
description: Managed MySQL, PostgreSQL and SQL Server databases with automated backups, high availability and read replicas.

title: Cloud TPU
description: Google's tensor processing unit accelerators, offered as VMs, slices and pods for training and serving large models.

title: Colab Enterprise
description: Managed Colab notebooks with shared runtimes and IAM, used both on Agent Platform and as the notebook engine inside BigQuery Studio.

title: Connected Sheets
description: Lets Google Sheets users analyse BigQuery and Looker data with pivots, formulas and charts that run in the source rather than in the sheet.

title: Conversational Analytics in Looker
description: Gemini-based agents that answer natural-language questions over LookML Explores and dashboards, grounded in the semantic model.

title: Data Agent Kit
description: IDE extension that connects coding agents and developers to Google Cloud data services through their remote MCP servers.

title: Data Labeling on Agent Platform
description: Manages labelling of image, video, text and tabular datasets by human labellers for supervised training on Agent Platform.

title: Dataflow ML
description: Beam transforms such as RunInference and MLTransform that run model inference and feature preprocessing, including embeddings, inside batch and streaming Dataflow pipelines.

title: Dataflow templates
description: Google-provided and custom Flex templates, plus the visual job builder, for running common ingestion and transformation pipelines without writing Beam code.

title: Dataform
description: Develops, tests, version-controls and runs SQL transformation workflows in BigQuery, defined in SQLX with dependencies resolved automatically.

title: Dataproc Metastore
description: Fully managed Apache Hive metastore for Spark, Hive and Trino workloads on Google Cloud.

title: Datastream
description: Serverless change data capture and replication from MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle, SQL Server, Spanner, MongoDB and Salesforce into BigQuery, Lakehouse Iceberg tables or Cloud Storage.

title: Eventarc
description: Routes events from Google Cloud services, audit logs, Cloud Storage and Pub/Sub to Cloud Run, Workflows and other targets.

title: Experiments on Agent Platform
description: Tracks parameters, metrics and artefacts of training runs and pipeline runs so they can be compared, with a managed TensorBoard for visualisation.

title: Firestore
description: Serverless document database for web, mobile and server applications, with real-time listeners, vector search and an edition compatible with the MongoDB API.

title: Gemini Enterprise
description: Employee-facing agent platform that combines enterprise search over connected applications, prebuilt and custom agents and Gemini chat under company permissions.

title: Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform
description: Google Cloud's platform, formerly Vertex AI, for building, deploying and governing ML models, generative AI applications and agents.

title: Gemini in BigQuery
description: Gemini assistance in BigQuery for generating, completing, explaining and fixing SQL and Python, and for generating dataset insights.

title: Gemini models on Agent Platform
description: Hosted access to Google's Gemini multimodal, embedding, image and speech models through Agent Platform APIs with pay-as-you-go, priority or provisioned throughput.

title: Gen AI evals on Agent Platform
formerly: Gen AI evaluation service;Gen AI evaluation service on Vertex AI
description: Evaluates model and agent outputs with computed metrics, model-based judges and rubrics, offline, against simulated users or as online monitoring.

title: Google Agent Development Kit
description: Open-source framework for writing single- and multi-agent applications with tools, memory and evaluation, deployable to Agent Runtime, Cloud Run or GKE.

title: Google Cloud Agent Gateway
description: Gateway that sits between agents, models and tools to enforce identity, policy, content screening and network controls on agent traffic.

title: Google Cloud Agent Observability
description: Traces, logs, metrics and topology views of agent runs, tool calls and model calls on Agent Platform, built on Cloud Observability.

title: Google Cloud Agent Registry
description: Inventory of the agents, tools and MCP servers in an organisation, used to register, discover and govern them.
