description: Tooling in BDC for creating, modelling and managing customer-defined data products with SQL or visual transformations, schema, lineage, versioning and lifecycle states.

title: SAP Business Data Cloud data products
description: SAP-managed, curated datasets with business metadata for core processes in SAP Cloud ERP, SuccessFactors and other applications, populated automatically from the source systems.

title: SAP Business Warehouse in SAP Business Data Cloud
description: Hosted SAP BW in BDC whose Data Product Generator turns BW InfoProvider data into data products in the BDC object store for Datasphere and Databricks to use.

title: SAP BW/4HANA
description: SAP's on-premises data warehouse application on SAP HANA, with modelled InfoProviders, extractors for SAP sources and query design for BI.

title: SAP Data Intelligence Cloud
description: SAP's earlier pipeline, orchestration and metadata service for integrating SAP and non-SAP data and running ML pipelines.

title: SAP Databricks
description: SAP-sold and SAP-managed Databricks workspace embedded in BDC, for notebooks, Spark pipelines, serverless SQL and ML over SAP data products shared with Delta Sharing.

title: SAP Datasphere
description: SAP's cloud data warehouse and data fabric service for integrating, modelling, federating and governing SAP and non-SAP data in isolated spaces with business semantics.

title: SAP Datasphere catalog and Data Marketplace
description: Catalogue for discovering and describing assets across Datasphere and connected systems, with glossary terms and KPIs, plus a marketplace for publishing and subscribing to data products.

title: SAP Datasphere replication flows
description: Datasphere feature that copies tables and CDS views from SAP and other sources in initial and delta mode into Datasphere or into external targets such as object stores, Kafka and cloud warehouses.

title: SAP HANA Cloud
description: Managed in-memory, multi-model database on SAP BTP for transactional and analytical work across relational, document, spatial, graph, time-series and vector data.

title: SAP HANA Cloud knowledge graph engine
description: RDF triple store with SPARQL in SAP HANA Cloud, which can generate graphs automatically from database metadata for semantic search and agent grounding.

title: SAP HANA Cloud vector engine
description: Vector data type, similarity functions and indexes in SAP HANA Cloud for semantic search and retrieval next to business data.

title: SAP HANA Cloud, data lake
description: Low-cost storage tier of SAP HANA Cloud with data lake Files for object storage and a data lake Relational Engine for SQL over large, colder datasets.

title: SAP Integration Suite
description: SAP BTP integration platform for process integration, API management, B2B and EDI exchange and event brokering between SAP and third-party applications.

title: SAP Joule and Joule agents
description: SAP's AI assistant across its applications, with agents (marketed in 2026 as Joule Assistants) that carry out multi-step business tasks under the user's authorisations.

title: SAP Joule Studio
aliases: Joule Studio;Joule Studio in SAP Build
description: Capability in SAP Build for building Joule skills and custom agents, from no-code to pro-code, with model choice, tool access and connection to MCP servers.

title: SAP Knowledge Graph
description: SAP-managed graph of business entities, fields and relationships across SAP applications that gives Joule and custom agents business context.

title: SAP Landscape Transformation Replication Server
description: Trigger-based replication server that captures changes from SAP ABAP systems and other databases and applies them in near real time to HANA or other targets.

title: SAP Master Data Governance
description: Application for central creation, consolidation and governed maintenance of master data with workflows, validation rules and quality monitoring, on S/4HANA or as a cloud edition on BTP.

title: SAP Snowflake
description: SAP-sold and SAP-operated Snowflake offering added to BDC as a solution extension, sharing SAP data products with Snowflake in both directions without copying.

title: Apache Iceberg tables in Snowflake
description: Tables stored as Parquet files with Apache Iceberg metadata, managed either by Snowflake as catalogue or by an external catalogue, in customer storage or in Snowflake storage.

title: Data mirroring for Snowflake Postgres
description: Continuously replicates Postgres tables or whole schemas into Snowflake tables from the write-ahead log, with sub-minute lag and source transaction boundaries kept.

title: dbt Projects on Snowflake
description: Deploys, runs, schedules and monitors dbt projects as Snowflake objects on a dbt Core or dbt Fusion runtime that Snowflake manages, developed in Workspaces or from Git.

title: Observe by Snowflake
description: An observability platform for logs, metrics and traces, built on a Snowflake lakehouse and available standalone or paid for with Snowflake credits.

title: pandas on Snowflake
description: A Modin-based pandas API that turns pandas operations on Snowflake data into SQL, and chooses per operation whether to run them locally or in Snowflake (hybrid execution).

title: pg_lake
description: An open-source Postgres extension from Snowflake that reads and writes Iceberg tables and Parquet files in object storage from Postgres.

title: SnowConvert AI
description: A migration tool that assesses and converts SQL code and objects from Teradata, Oracle, SQL Server, Redshift, Synapse, BigQuery, Databricks SQL and other platforms to Snowflake.

title: Snowflake access control (RBAC and database roles)
description: A hierarchy of account roles, database roles and application roles that hold privileges on securable objects, with secondary roles and managed access schemas.

title: Snowflake Access History
description: An ACCOUNT_USAGE view that records which columns each query read and which objects it wrote, including through views and policies.

title: Snowflake ACCOUNT_USAGE and ORGANIZATION_USAGE
description: Shared SNOWFLAKE database schemas that expose query, login, metering, storage, access, task, AI and billing history as views, for one account or the whole organisation.

title: Snowflake Adaptive Compute
description: A warehouse type (adaptive warehouses) for which Snowflake decides the resources for each query, so you do not set a size, multi-cluster settings or suspend policies.

title: Snowflake aggregation policies
description: Require queries on a protected table to aggregate rows into groups above a minimum size, at row or entity level, so individual records cannot be returned.

title: Snowflake AI Observability
description: Tracing, cost tracking and batch evaluation for agents, Cortex Search, CoCo and custom TruLens-instrumented apps, stored in an account event table and viewed in Snowsight.

title: Snowflake AI-generated descriptions
description: Uses Cortex models to draft descriptions of tables, views and columns in Snowsight for owners to review and save as comments.

title: Snowflake alerts and notifications
description: Scheduled or event-driven conditions written in SQL that run an action, such as sending email, webhook or cloud-queue notifications, when data meets them.

title: Snowflake authentication (SSO, OAuth, key pair, PATs, workload identity federation)
description: Authenticates users and services through SAML SSO, Snowflake or external OAuth, key pairs, programmatic access tokens, MFA and workload identity federation with cloud identities.

title: Snowflake backups
description: Point-in-time, zero-copy backups of tables, schemas and databases, managed through backup sets and backup policies, with optional retention locks and legal holds.

title: Snowflake budgets
description: Monthly credit limits for the account or for custom groups of objects (including by tag) that forecast spend, send notifications and can run stored procedures, for example to suspend warehouses.

title: Snowflake bulk loading (COPY INTO <table>)
description: Loads staged files in bulk into tables on a warehouse, tracking which files were loaded so they are not loaded twice.

title: Snowflake catalog-linked databases
description: Databases linked to an external Iceberg REST catalogue (for example AWS Glue, Unity Catalog, Open Catalog, BigLake or S3 Tables) that discover and sync remote namespaces and tables automatically for querying and writing.

title: Snowflake CLI
description: An open-source command-line tool for running SQL and for building, testing and deploying Snowflake apps, Snowpark code, Streamlit apps, dbt and DCM projects from local machines and CI pipelines.

title: Snowflake clustering keys and Automatic Clustering
description: Lets you declare clustering columns on large tables, then reorganises micro-partitions in the background to keep them well clustered so pruning stays effective.

title: Snowflake CoCo
description: An AI coding agent, available in Snowsight, as a CLI, as a desktop app and in VS Code, that uses Snowflake skills and MCP tools to explore data, write SQL, and build pipelines, dbt projects and apps.

title: Snowflake Connector for Kafka
description: A Kafka Connect sink connector that loads topics into Snowflake tables using Snowpipe Streaming.

title: Snowflake Container Runtime for ML
description: A prebuilt CPU and GPU ML environment on Snowpark Container Services, with distributed data loading, training and hyperparameter tuning built on Ray.

title: Snowflake Copilot
description: An SQL assistant in Snowsight that generates and explains queries from natural language.

title: Snowflake Cortex Agents
description: Schema-level agent objects that plan, call tools such as Cortex Analyst, Cortex Search, custom procedures, sandboxed Python code execution and web search, and answer with governed data.

title: Snowflake Cortex AI Function Studio
description: A Snowsight workspace for designing prompts for Cortex AI Functions, evaluating them against labelled data and optimising them.

title: Snowflake Cortex AI Functions
description: SQL functions such as AI_COMPLETE, AI_CLASSIFY, AI_FILTER, AI_AGG, AI_SUMMARIZE_AGG, AI_EMBED, AI_SENTIMENT, AI_TRANSLATE, AI_TRANSCRIBE and AI_REDACT that apply hosted models to columns and files.

title: Snowflake Cortex AI Functions for documents (AI_PARSE_DOCUMENT, AI_EXTRACT)
description: AI_PARSE_DOCUMENT turns PDFs and images into text and layout, and AI_EXTRACT pulls named fields, tables and entities out of documents.

title: Snowflake Cortex AI Gateway
description: A single governed endpoint for AI clients that routes model calls, records traces and token use, and attributes spend to teams and users under budgets and quotas.

title: Snowflake Cortex AI Guardrails
description: Runtime checks that detect prompt injection and jailbreak attempts, including indirect injection in tool outputs, for Cortex Agents, CoWork and CoCo.

title: Snowflake Cortex Analyst
description: Turns natural-language questions into SQL over semantic views and returns the answers, through a REST API or as an agent tool.

title: Snowflake Cortex Fine-tuning
description: Builds parameter-efficient fine-tuned adaptors for supported base models from training data in Snowflake, for inference through AI_COMPLETE.

title: Snowflake Cortex Knowledge Extensions
description: Cortex Search services shared as Marketplace or private listings, so a consumer's agents and RAG apps can search a provider's content, with citations.

title: Snowflake Cortex REST API
description: REST endpoints, including chat-completions-style APIs, that give applications access to the large language models hosted in Snowflake's security boundary.

title: Snowflake Cortex Search
description: A managed hybrid vector and keyword search service, with reranking, that embeds, indexes and refreshes text from a query or stage on a target lag.

title: Snowflake cost anomaly detection
description: Flags days when account or organisation consumption falls outside the expected range, with optional anomaly monitors scoped by tags or service types.

title: Snowflake CoWork
description: A conversational agent application for business users that answers questions over structured and unstructured data, runs deep research, and produces artefacts, documents and scheduled automations.

title: Snowflake Data Clean Rooms
description: Collaborations defined in YAML, in which owners, data providers and analysis runners combine data through approved templates without exposing raw rows to one another.

title: Snowflake data lineage (Snowsight lineage)
description: Records table and column lineage from DML, CTAS and view dependencies, plus ML lineage across datasets, feature views, models and monitors, shown as a graph in Catalog Explorer.

title: Snowflake data quality monitoring (data metric functions)
description: Schedules system and custom data metric functions on tables and views, compares results with expectations, and detects volume and freshness anomalies, with results in Snowsight.

title: Snowflake data unloading (COPY INTO <location>)
description: Writes query results or tables to files in internal or external stages as CSV, JSON or Parquet, optionally partitioned.

title: Snowflake DCM Projects
description: Database Change Management projects that declare the desired state of databases, schemas, tables, dynamic tables, views, warehouses, roles, grants and data quality checks in SQL DEFINE files, then plan and deploy the changes.

title: Snowflake differential privacy
description: Privacy policies that add calibrated noise to aggregate results on protected tables and track each analyst's cumulative privacy loss against a budget.

title: Snowflake drivers, connectors and SQL API
description: JDBC, ODBC, Python, Go, .NET and Node.js drivers, the Spark connector and a REST SQL API for connecting tools and applications to Snowflake.

title: Snowflake Dynamic Tables
description: Tables defined by a query and a target lag that Snowflake keeps refreshed, incrementally where possible, working out dependency order across chains of dynamic tables.

title: Snowflake Extension for Visual Studio Code
description: An IDE extension for connecting to Snowflake, running SQL and Snowpark code, and using CoCo from a local editor.

title: Snowflake external lineage
description: Accepts OpenLineage COMPLETE events through a REST endpoint, so tools such as dbt and Airflow can add lineage from outside Snowflake to the lineage graph.

title: Snowflake external network access (external access integrations)
description: Lets UDFs, procedures and container services call approved external endpoints over the network, using network rules and secrets, for example to pull data from REST APIs.

title: Snowflake external tables
description: Read-only tables over files in external stages, with optional automatic metadata refresh, so data in a lake can be queried without loading it.

title: Snowflake Fail-safe
description: Keeps a further non-configurable 7 days of historical data for permanent tables after Time Travel ends, recoverable only by Snowflake Support after a disaster.

title: Snowflake Feature Store
description: Python APIs and objects for defining entities and feature views (as Dynamic Tables or views), generating point-in-time correct training sets and retrieving features for batch inference.

title: Snowflake generation 2 standard warehouses
description: The newer generation of standard warehouses, running on faster hardware with optimisations for DELETE, UPDATE, MERGE and table scans.

title: Snowflake geospatial data types and functions
description: GEOGRAPHY and GEOMETRY types with spatial functions, H3 indexing and spatial joins in SQL.

title: Snowflake Git integration (Git repository objects)
description: Syncs remote Git repositories into Snowflake as repository clones, so code can be run with EXECUTE IMMEDIATE FROM and Workspaces, notebooks and Streamlit apps can commit and push.

title: Snowflake Horizon Catalog
description: Snowflake's built-in catalogue and governance layer, covering object discovery, tagging, policies, quality, lineage, access history and Iceberg catalogue services for Snowflake and external data.

title: Snowflake Horizon Context
description: A layer of Horizon Catalog that gathers external metadata and lineage, enriches it with semantics, popularity and AI descriptions, and exposes it to agents and BI tools through search and MCP.

title: Snowflake Horizon Iceberg REST Catalog API
description: An Apache Polaris-based Iceberg REST catalogue endpoint in each account that lets Spark, Trino, Flink, DuckDB, PyIceberg and other engines read and write Snowflake-managed Iceberg tables under Snowflake RBAC.

title: Snowflake hybrid tables (Unistore)
description: A row-oriented table type with enforced primary, unique and foreign keys, indexes and row locking, for low-latency point reads and writes in the same engine as analytical tables.

title: Snowflake Intent-Driven Governance
description: A review-first CoCo workflow that turns a governance goal stated in plain language into a scope, a governance specification and SQL for tags and protections, which a person approves before it runs.

title: Snowflake interactive tables and interactive warehouses
description: A table type and a matching warehouse type built for sub-second, highly concurrent queries such as user-facing dashboards and data APIs.

title: Snowflake Internal Marketplace (organisational listings)
description: A private marketplace inside a Snowflake organisation where teams publish organisational listings as data products for discovery and access requests by other accounts.

title: Snowflake listings (with Cross-Cloud Auto-Fulfillment)
description: Package a share, app or service with descriptive metadata as a data product for chosen accounts, replicating it automatically to consumers in other regions and clouds.

title: Snowflake Marketplace
description: A public catalogue where providers publish free, paid or trial listings of data, Native Apps, Cortex Knowledge Extensions and agents, and consumers subscribe to them.

title: Snowflake masking policies
description: Schema-level policies that mask, tokenise or reveal column values at query time depending on role, other context or tags, including external tokenisation through external functions.

title: Snowflake materialized views
description: Stores the results of a single-table query and keeps them up to date automatically in the background, so queries read precomputed results.

title: Snowflake micro-partitioned table storage
description: Stores standard tables in immutable, compressed, columnar micro-partitions with per-partition statistics that Snowflake manages, giving ACID transactions and partition pruning.

title: Snowflake ML Experiments
description: Records runs with parameters, metrics, artefacts and logs inside experiments, with autologging for common libraries and side-by-side comparison in Snowsight.

title: Snowflake ML Functions
description: SQL-callable model classes for time-series forecasting, anomaly detection, classification and top insights, which train and run without ML code.

title: Snowflake ML Jobs
description: Submits Python functions, files or code bundles from any IDE or from SQL to run as jobs on Container Runtime compute pools, including on multiple nodes.

title: Snowflake ML Observability (model monitors)
description: Model monitor objects that compute drift, performance and statistical metrics from logged inference data, with dashboards and threshold alerts.

title: Snowflake Model Registry
description: Stores versioned models trained in Snowflake or elsewhere as schema-level objects with metadata, metrics and aliases, and runs their methods from SQL or Python for batch inference.

title: Snowflake Model Serving in Snowpark Container Services
description: Deploys registry models as autoscaling CPU or GPU inference services with HTTP endpoints, with gateway-based traffic splitting for shadow and canary releases.

title: Snowflake multi-cluster warehouses
description: Adds and removes clusters of the same size automatically, according to a scaling policy, to absorb bursts of concurrent queries without queuing.

title: Snowflake Native App Framework
description: Packages data, code, Streamlit UIs, containers, agents and MCP servers as applications that consumers install and run in their own accounts through listings.

title: Snowflake native connectors (Snowflake Connectors for ServiceNow, Google Analytics, SharePoint, PostgreSQL and MySQL)
description: Connectors packaged as Snowflake Native Apps that ingest and refresh data from SaaS applications and databases incrementally, some using a customer-run agent for change data capture.

title: Snowflake network policies and network rules
description: Restrict which IP ranges, VPC endpoints or private endpoints can reach an account or user, and which external destinations workloads can reach.

title: Snowflake Notebooks in Workspaces
description: Jupyter-compatible notebooks in Snowsight Workspaces that run on Container Runtime CPU or GPU compute, with Git integration, a terminal and scheduling.

title: Snowflake object tagging
description: Schema-level tags with allowed values that are attached to objects and columns, inherited down the hierarchy, and used for classification, cost attribution and tag-based policies.

title: Snowflake Online Feature Store
description: Syncs feature views to a low-latency online store and serves them by key through a REST API, with stream and real-time feature views for sub-minute freshness.

title: Snowflake Open Catalog
description: A separate managed Apache Polaris service that acts as an Iceberg REST catalogue with central access control for Iceberg tables shared across engines.

title: Snowflake Open Data Sharing
description: Shares Iceberg tables as live, read-only data with external consumers outside Snowflake, who read them through standard Iceberg REST Catalog APIs using a programmatic access token.

title: Snowflake Openflow
description: A managed integration service, built on Apache NiFi, that runs prebuilt and custom connectors for databases, SaaS, streams and unstructured content in batch or streaming mode.

title: Snowflake organisations
description: Group multiple Snowflake accounts across regions and clouds under one organisation for account creation, organisation-wide usage views, organisation users and organisational listings.

title: Snowflake persisted query results (result cache)
description: Returns the stored result of an identical earlier query, for 24 hours and up to 31 days with reuse, when the underlying data has not changed, without using warehouse compute.

title: Snowflake Postgres
description: Fully managed PostgreSQL instances, on versions 16 to 18, created and governed from Snowflake, running on dedicated Snowflake-managed machines with PgBouncer pooling and private networking.

title: Snowflake private connectivity (AWS PrivateLink, Azure Private Link, Google Cloud Private Service Connect)
description: Connects clients, internal stages and Snowflake-hosted endpoints to Snowflake over the cloud provider's private network rather than the public internet.

title: Snowflake projection policies
description: Stop a column from being returned in query output while still allowing it in joins, filters and aggregations.

title: Snowflake Query Acceleration Service
description: Offloads parts of large scans and filters in eligible queries to shared serverless compute, so outlier queries finish faster without enlarging the warehouse.

title: Snowflake Query History, Query Profile and query insights
description: Snowsight views of query history, operator-level execution plans and automatic insights, used to diagnose slow or expensive queries.

title: Snowflake replication and failover groups
description: Replicate databases, users, roles, warehouses, policies and integrations to accounts in other regions or clouds, with promotion on failover and client redirect through connection objects.

title: Snowflake resource monitors
description: Credit quotas on warehouses or the whole account that notify or suspend warehouses when thresholds are reached.

title: Snowflake row access policies
description: Schema-level policies that decide, using the querying role and mapping tables, which rows of a table or view a query returns.

title: Snowflake Search Optimization Service
description: Builds and maintains a persistent search access path on chosen tables and columns, so point lookups, substring, semi-structured, geospatial and full-text SEARCH queries skip most micro-partitions.

title: Snowflake secrets
description: Schema-level secret objects that hold credentials, OAuth tokens and keys for integrations, UDFs, Openflow and container services, so code does not contain them.

title: Snowflake Secure Data Sharing
description: Shares live, read-only database objects with other Snowflake accounts through shares, without copying data, with consumers paying for their own compute.

title: Snowflake semantic views
description: Schema-level objects that define logical tables, relationships, facts, dimensions and metrics, queried with SQL and used by Cortex Analyst, agents and BI tools.

title: Snowflake semi-structured data types (VARIANT, OBJECT, ARRAY)
description: Stores JSON, Avro, ORC, Parquet and XML in VARIANT, OBJECT and ARRAY columns, extracting columns for pruning, and queries them with path notation and FLATTEN.

title: Snowflake sensitive data classification
description: Scans tables in databases with a classification profile, assigns semantic and privacy categories to sensitive columns, and can map them to your own tags automatically.

title: Snowflake stages and directory tables
description: Internal and external stages hold files in object storage, and directory tables catalogue the staged files with metadata so unstructured content can be listed, governed and processed with SQL.

title: Snowflake storage lifecycle policies
description: Schema-level policies that archive table rows to cheaper COOL or COLD tiers, or delete them permanently, according to conditions such as age.

title: Snowflake streams
description: Track inserts, updates and deletes on tables, views and other objects since an offset, so downstream jobs process only the changes.

title: Snowflake synthetic data generation
description: The GENERATE_SYNTHETIC_DATA procedure creates statistically similar tables, with the same column names and types, from up to five source tables without linking output rows to real records.

title: Snowflake tasks and task graphs
description: Run SQL, procedures or code on a schedule, in dependency graphs, or when a stream has new data, on serverless or user-managed compute.

title: Snowflake Terraform provider
description: A Terraform provider for managing Snowflake accounts, warehouses, databases, roles, grants and policies as code.

title: Snowflake Time Travel
description: Queries, clones or undrops tables, schemas and databases as they were at an earlier point within a retention period of up to 90 days.

title: Snowflake time-series functions (ASOF JOIN, TIME_SLICE, RESAMPLE)
description: SQL constructs for aligning, bucketing and joining time-stamped data, including ASOF JOIN and gap filling.

title: Snowflake Trail (event tables, logging, tracing and metrics)
description: Collects logs, OpenTelemetry-style traces and metrics from UDFs, procedures, Snowpark, Native Apps, container services and pipelines into event tables, with Snowsight dashboards.

title: Snowflake Tri-Secret Secure
description: Combines a Snowflake-maintained key with a customer-managed key in the cloud provider's KMS to create the composite master key for account data, so revoking the customer key makes data unreadable.

title: Snowflake Trust Center
description: Runs scanner packages (Security Essentials, CIS Benchmarks, Threat Intelligence, AI Security) against accounts and reports violations, detections and at-risk entities.

title: Snowflake Universal Search
description: Searches object metadata across the account, the Snowflake Marketplace and the Internal Marketplace in Snowsight, in natural language, filtered by the user's privileges.

title: Snowflake user-defined functions and stored procedures
description: Custom scalar, table and aggregate functions and stored procedures written in SQL, Snowflake Scripting, JavaScript, Python, Java or Scala that run inside Snowflake.

title: Snowflake virtual warehouses
description: Named clusters of compute, sized from X-Small to 6X-Large, that run SQL and Snowpark workloads against shared storage and suspend and resume automatically.

title: Snowflake zero-copy cloning
description: Creates instant writable copies of tables, schemas or databases that share micro-partitions with the source until either side changes.

title: Snowflake-managed MCP server
description: A Snowflake object that exposes Cortex Agents, Cortex Analyst, Cortex Search, SQL execution and custom functions as Model Context Protocol tools to external AI clients under RBAC.

title: Snowpark
description: DataFrame and function APIs for Python, Java and Scala that push processing down into Snowflake warehouses as SQL, plus runtimes for running that code in the engine.

title: Snowpark Connect for Apache Spark
description: Runs existing Spark DataFrame and Spark SQL code on Snowflake compute through the Spark Connect protocol, so there is no Spark cluster to manage.

title: Snowpark Container Services
description: Runs OCI container images as long-running services or finite jobs on Snowflake-managed compute pools, including GPU nodes, inside the account's security boundary.

title: Snowpark-optimized warehouses
description: Warehouses with much more memory per node, and configurable CPU architecture, for memory-intensive Snowpark, UDF and single-node ML training work.

title: Snowpipe
description: A serverless pipe that loads files continuously from stages as they arrive, triggered by cloud storage event notifications or REST calls.

title: Snowpipe Streaming
description: Ingests rows directly into tables through SDKs (Java, Python, Node.js) or a REST API, with no files, making data queryable within seconds.

title: Snowsight dashboards
description: Simple dashboards built from charts and tables of query results in Snowsight, shared with other Snowflake users.

title: Snowsight Workspaces
description: A file-based editor in Snowsight for SQL, Python, notebooks, dbt projects, Streamlit apps and semantic views, with Git integration, sharing and AI code suggestions.

title: Streamlit in Snowflake
description: Hosts Streamlit Python apps as Snowflake objects, on warehouse or container runtimes, with access governed by Snowflake roles.

title: Virtual Private Snowflake (VPS)
description: The highest Snowflake edition, which runs a dedicated, isolated Snowflake deployment for a single customer, with its own metadata store and compute.

title: Teradata AI Studio
description: Umbrella environment for in-database analytics, open Python compute, ModelOps, vector storage and agent tooling on the Teradata platform.

title: Teradata Autonomous Knowledge Platform
description: Umbrella name for Teradata's platform of database, open-format storage access, analytics, vector and agent services, run either as Teradata Cloud or Teradata Factory.

title: Teradata Backup, Archive and Restore and Data Mover
aliases: Teradata BAR;Teradata Data Mover;Teradata DSA;Data Stream Architecture
description: Tools for backing up Teradata systems, restoring them, and copying tables and databases between systems for disaster recovery or environment refresh.

title: Teradata Bring Your Own Model (BYOM)
description: Database functions that score externally trained models, such as ONNX and PMML, in parallel inside Teradata without exporting data.

title: Teradata Cloud
description: Teradata-managed deployment of the platform on AWS, Azure and Google Cloud, combining always-on active compute with elastic compute that scales on demand over database and object-storage data.

title: Teradata Database
description: Shared-nothing MPP SQL database engine that underlies all Teradata deployments, with mixed-workload management, temporal tables and support for semi-structured data.

title: Teradata Database security (roles, row-level security, encryption)
description: Built-in database controls for role-based privileges, row-level security constraints, column masking through views and functions, access logging and encryption.

title: Teradata Elastic Python Compute
description: Managed, distributed Python environment based on Ray that runs ML, AI and data engineering code on CPUs or GPUs next to Teradata Database and open-format tables.

title: Teradata Enterprise AgentStack
description: Suite for building, running and governing AI agents on Teradata, made up of AgentBuilder, Enterprise MCP, AgentEngine and AgentOps.

title: Teradata Enterprise MCP
description: Governed MCP server that exposes Teradata data, metadata, analytics, vector store and administration functions to AI agents as tools, bound to each user's identity and database roles.

title: Teradata Enterprise Vector Store
description: Vector storage and retrieval inside the Teradata platform, with hybrid keyword and semantic search across structured data and embeddings of text, images and audio.

title: Teradata Fabric
description: Query federation layer that joins data across Teradata systems and other engines such as Hive, Spark SQL, Oracle and BigQuery, pushing processing to where the data sits.

title: Teradata Factory
description: On-premises Teradata system on Dell compute and storage with NVIDIA GPUs, running warehouse, lakehouse and AI workloads together inside the customer's data centre.

title: Teradata in-database analytics functions
description: Large library of SQL functions for data preparation, statistics, machine learning, time-series and path analysis that run in parallel inside the database, also callable from Python and R.

title: Teradata ModelOps
description: Model lifecycle service that validates, deploys and monitors in-database and imported models, with drift alerts, a feature catalogue and audit trails of the data used.

title: Teradata Open Table Format support (Apache Iceberg and Delta Lake)
description: Ability for the Teradata engine to read and write Apache Iceberg and Delta Lake tables in object storage through external catalogues, alongside Native Object Store access to Parquet, CSV and JSON files.

title: Teradata Tera
description: Agentic workspace in which Teradata agents analyse data, write code, tune queries and run multi-step data tasks, grounded in governed metadata, lineage and policies.

title: Teradata Viewpoint
description: Web console for monitoring Teradata systems, queries, sessions and workloads and for managing workload rules.
